messages:
Maya (support): heads up — acme-corp just escalated. p95/p99 spiked after a runtime push ~15:09 UTC. They say many requests are hitting 2s+ p99 and some timed out. stack: hosted inference, model redwood/gpt-7b-quant, default route. Can eng-runtime triage?
Alex (eng-runtime): on it. seeing an automatic rollout at 15:09 from BuildBot -> runtime 2026.03.15-build-512. That build turned on FlashAttention + SDPA auto-tuning heuristics in the kernel selector.
BuildBot: deploy: rollout complete -> prod.us-west-2 @ 2026-03-15T15:09:12Z (build-512) :rocket:
Maya (support): customer timeline: p99 was ~460ms before 15:09, jumped to ~2.1s after. p95 from 220ms -> 700ms. They've got live product users; marking as high priority.
SRE-Oncall (bot): incident assigned -> severity: high. channel: #incidents. paging eng-runtime.
Alex (eng-runtime): quick check on metrics — here's a snippet from our edge metrics around that window:```
region=us-west-2 model=gpt-7b-quant p95=700 p99=2100 request_count=1342
region=us-east-1 model=gpt-7b-quant p95=230 p99=490 request_count=987
kernel_choice=flash_attention_blocked kernel_version=2.4.0
queue_len_avg=0.9 batch_size_median=1
```
Alex (eng-runtime): interesting — only us-west-2 shows the tail. same build rolled globally but traffic patterns differ (more small-batch traffic in us-west for acme). Kernel selector picked "flash_attention_blocked" variant. For batch=1/seq>=512 that kernel has higher launch/setup overhead and can increase tail.
Jamie (eng-ml): to add: FlashAttention improves throughput for larger batches/seqs but can worsen latency tail for small-batch, long-context requests because of extra kernel workspace allocation + async syncs. SDPA heuristic changes also favor different indexing which may add extra memory ops.
Carla (eng-sre): mitigation attempt: I flipped per-model flag to disable FlashAttention for acme's route and pinned kernel_version to 2.3.3 for that tenant. Doing that now:```
# per-tenant runtime override
redwoodctl runtime set --tenant acme-corp --model redwood/gpt-7b-quant --flag FLASH_ATTENTION=false --pin-kernel 2.3.3
```
Carla (eng-sre): after override (15:32) p99 on their route dropped to ~380ms, p95 ~240ms. Confirmed by customer — temporary relief. :relieved:
Dmitri (eng-infra): why did the selector pick that blocked flash kernel in us-west only? build-512 includes a new kernel-autotune change: kernel_selector now prefers estimated throughput over tail latency when predicted throughput_gain > 15%. For small-batch traffic the estimator was noisy and mispredicted. I'll revert that autotune commit for the next hotfix.
Alex (eng-runtime): repro steps I'm using locally to reproduce the tail:```
# reproduce tail with our perf tool
./inference-bench --model redwood/gpt-7b-quant --seq-len 1024 --batch-size 1 --requests 5000 --concurrency 5 --flags FLASH_ATTENTION=on SDPA=auto
# collect kernel selection log: /tmp/kernel_choices.log
```
Jamie (eng-ml): additional repro: run with env var to force kernel variants and measure p99:```
export FORCE_KERNEL=flash_blocked ./inference-bench --batch-size 1 --seq-len 1024 --requests 2000
# observe p99 jump compared to FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_sdpa
```
Alex (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: the new autotuner (build-512) changed the scoring function so for some workloads it prefers flash_blocked kernel. For very small batches, kernel launch/setup overhead dominates; on GPUs with slightly different driver/clock (us-west fleet) this overhead is larger -> tail.
Carla (eng-sre): immediate mitigation summary applied: per-tenant override for acme + pinned kernel 2.3.3. We also increased per-route timeout buffer for a short window to avoid timeouts while we hotfix.
Maya (support): customer confirmed immediate improvement — thanks team. They're okay with temporary pin while you ship a long-term fix.
Dmitri (eng-infra): next actions I propose: 1) emergency hotfix to revert autotune scoring in runtime (rollback change in build-512) and cut build-513 with scoring revert; 2) add a kernel-selection telemetry tag (kernel_choice, predicted_gain, scoring_reason) to every request for 24h; 3) add a per-model policy: prefer latency-optimized kernel when median batch_size <=4 OR seq_len >=512 AND p99 sensitivity threshold.
Alex (eng-runtime): timeline: I'll prepare hotfix PR now. If Carla can keep the tenant override, we can push hotfix to canary and monitor. We should also ship a CLI tool to flip per-model FlashAttention quickly.
Jamie (eng-ml): long-term: update tuning rules — don't use raw predicted throughput gain; include an estimate of launch overhead and batch-size conditioned penalty. We'll add small-batch microbenchmarks to the CI autotuner.
Carla (eng-sre): monitors/alerts updated: added alert if p99 increases >50% in region post-deploy for any model. Also added runbook steps: how to pin kernel or disable flash per-route.
Alex (eng-runtime): PR opened: runtime#987 (revert-autotune-score). Canaries scheduled to prod.us-west-2 at 16:10 UTC. Will post results.
BuildBot: ci/build: build-513 created from runtime#987, tests green.
Dmitri (eng-infra): small note — driver version differences on us-west fleet exacerbated additional kernel workspace allocation time. We'll roll matching driver updates, but that's medium-term.
Maya (support): thanks — I'll keep acme updated and close the escalation once build-513 is verified. please ping here when canary is stable.
Alex (eng-runtime): canary finished: p99 back to baseline (~480ms) in canary region. Rolling to rest of us-west now. Will monitor 30m.
Carla (eng-sre): post-rollout check: all affected tenant routes show p99 within expected bounds. Closing immediate incident. Follow-ups: autotuner change reverted in release notes; ticket created to improve estimator and add microbenchmarks (ENG-1209).
Jamie (eng-ml): follow-up items for backlog: add small-batch microbenchmarks, per-kernel latency-tail instrumentation, and update autotune scoring.
Alex (eng-runtime): notes for postmortem: cause = autotuner scoring change + small-batch heavy traffic pattern in one region + minor driver perf variance. Mitigations = per-tenant override, pin kernel, revert autotune, telemetry to catch selection decisions.
Maya (support): closing loop with customer now. Great work everyone. :heart:
